repo.description:
Immich's **Locked folder** (hidden vault) is the most-private asset class: `visibility: locked` assets are hidden from the timeline and require the OWNER's PIN (an elevated session) to view. The code intends Locked assets to stay hidden even from PARTNERS - `timeBucketChecks` blocks Locked when `withPartners` is set, and `getUserIdsToSearch` carries the comment "Locked assets are personal. Never include partner IDs, regardless of A's elevated session."

Two endpoints break that boundary: both authorize the Locked case using only the CALLER's own elevated session plus a partner-broad access grant, never binding the target `userId` to the caller. A partner (any low-trust sharing relationship) with their OWN PIN can read another user's hidden-vault asset IDs, GPS coordinates, blur previews, timestamps, and counts. Runtime-verified end-to-end against `ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:release` (v3.0.3).

## Finding 1 (High) - partner reads victim's Locked timeline
`GET /api/timeline/bucket` and `GET /api/timeline/buckets` (`@Authenticated({permission: AssetRead, sharedLink:true})`) → `server/src/services/timeline.service.ts` `timeBucketChecks`:
```
if (dto.visibility === AssetVisibility.Locked) { requireElevatedPermission(auth); }   // caller's OWN session only
...
if (dto.userId) {
  await this.requireAccess({ auth, permission: Permission.TimelineRead, ids: [dto.userId] }); // partner-broad
  if (dto.visibility === AssetVisibility.Archive) {
    await this.requireAccess({ auth, permission: Permission.ArchiveRead, ids: [dto.userId] }); // Archive self-binds
  } // NO equivalent self-bind for Locked
}
```
`requireElevatedPermission` (`utils/access.ts`) validates only `auth.session?.hasElevatedPermission` - the ATTACKER's PIN session, not the owner of the target assets. `Permission.TimelineRead` admits partners (`access.timeline.checkPartnerAccess`). The Archive branch adds `ArchiveRead` (which only ever returns `auth.user.id`, self-restricting to the caller); Locked has no such guard. The repository then binds only `ownerId = dto.userId`, and `withDefaultVisibility` (which would exclude Locked) is skipped because `visibility` is passed explicitly.

Impact: cross-user disclosure of the victim's PIN-locked hidden-vault asset IDs, per-bucket counts, and metadata - GPS latitude/longitude, city, country, a thumbhash blur preview, timestamps, aspect ratio, favorite/trashed status, live-photo id. The full image itself is NOT reachable (partner AssetRead/AssetView correctly exclude Locked), so it is bounded to metadata + location + preview of the most sensitive asset class.

Runtime proof (v3.0.3), Alice=attacker, Bob=victim, Bob added Alice as partner, Bob's photo in Locked vault, Alice elevated her OWN session:
```
# control (boundary is real):
Alice(elevated) GET /timeline/buckets?userId=<random-non-partner>&visibility=locked  -> 400 (denied)
# attack:
Alice(elevated,partner) GET /timeline/buckets?userId=<BOB>&visibility=locked   -> 200 [{"timeBucket":"2026-01-01","count":1}]
Alice(elevated,partner) GET /timeline/bucket?userId=<BOB>&visibility=locked&timeBucket=2026-01-01&withCoordinates=true
   -> 200 { id:[<BOB's LOCKED asset>], visibility:["locked"], ownerId:[BOB], city/country/latitude/longitude/thumbhash/... }
# ceiling (image not reachable):
Alice GET /assets/<id> -> 400; /assets/<id>/thumbnail -> 400; /assets/<id>/original -> 404
```

## Finding 2 (Low, same root cause) - partner leaks victim's Locked count via search statistics
`POST /api/search/statistics` (`@Authenticated({permission: AssetStatistics})`) → `server/src/services/search.service.ts` `searchStatistics` calls `getUserIdsToSearch(auth)` WITHOUT `dto.visibility`, unlike its four siblings (`searchMetadata`/`searchRandom`/`searchLargeAssets`/`searchSmart`) which all pass it. `getUserIdsToSearch` only short-circuits to self-only `[auth.user.id]` when `visibility === Locked`; because visibility is omitted it falls through to `[auth.user.id, ...partnerIds]`, while `dto.visibility=locked` still reaches the repository.
```
Alice POST /api/search/statistics {"visibility":"locked"}  -> 200 {"total":1}   (Alice owns 0; the 1 is BOB's locked asset)
```
The DTO's date/city/camera filters make this a granular oracle over the hidden vault.

## Suggested fix (single root cause)
For `visibility === Locked`, bind scope to the caller only: in `timeBucketChecks`, require `dto.userId === auth.user.id` for Locked (mirror the Archive/`ArchiveRead` self-bind) so `TimelineRead` (partner-broad) can never authorize a Locked read of another user's timeline; in `searchStatistics`, pass `dto.visibility` into `getUserIdsToSearch(auth, dto.visibility)` like the four siblings and add the `requireElevatedPermission` guard.

Found via source review + runtime verification of `main` @ HEAD f2b0b69 (2026-07-20). Distinct from the published Immich advisories (album-name open-redirect, AssetShare add-owner-assets, shared-link password, OAuth hijack, etc.). Please credit "cyberkareem" (https://github.com/CyberKareem). Happy to help validate the fix.
repo.summary: Cross-user disclosure of a user's Locked (hidden-vault) assets to a partner via timeline-bucket and search-statistics endpoints
